target.title: fix(acpx): drain leased descendants when turns are aborted
target.body:
Refs #104847

## Current Status

**Draft.** The obsolete generic CLI/process-group patch has been removed. The current head is a single ACPX-focused commit (`457208666c72cd58b3fa6a39195de3f9c98dfa3c`) with public before/after macOS process evidence and a passing service-managed ownership proof. All changed-path type, lint, docs, extension-boundary, ACPX, ACP manager, and abort-feedback gates pass. This PR remains Draft pending maintainer confirmation of the fail-closed ACPX containment contract and current-head review.

## What Problem This Solves

Cancelling an ACP-backed turn could stop the visible reply while leaving an ACPX-owned worker alive after it detached from the wrapper's PPID tree. The existing ACPX reaper validated the wrapper lease but only walked current parent/child relationships, so `setsid`, double-fork, or a reparented headless worker could escape cleanup. The fast-abort path also logged ACP cleanup failures and could still report the normal abort success text.

## Why This Change Was Made

- ACP cancellation now always closes and evicts the cached runtime handle after the protocol-cancel attempt. A protocol-cancel failure cannot skip process cleanup; a successful close/drain still counts as a safe abort.
- ACPX cleanup combines the live PPID tree with inherited random lease ID and Gateway instance ID markers. Reparented descendants remain attributable after their PPID changes.
- POSIX inventory uses bounded `ps eww` output only for in-memory ownership matching and never logs the process environment. Windows uses `Win32_Process` PID/PPID inventory.
- Cleanup escalates from `SIGTERM` to `SIGKILL`, rechecks liveness, records surviving PIDs, and marks the lease `lost` when the scope does not drain.
- ACPX startup reaps stale open leases before registering the backend and fails closed if ownership cannot be verified or drained.
- `/stop` reports an explicit containment failure instead of “Agent was aborted” when ACP cleanup fails.
- Generic persistent `exec`/`process` background sessions are outside the ACPX lease path and retain their existing lifecycle.

## User Impact

Aborting an ACPX turn now closes the live ACP runtime and reaps lease-owned descendants even after ordinary session detachment/reparenting. Binding and session metadata remain available, so a later turn can reopen or resume. Operators receive a failure instead of false success if cleanup cannot be proven.

## Evidence

### Before: launchd/process-group boundary

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` proof:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29183003523
- Job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29183003523/job/86624023019
- Evidence branch: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/pull/3
- Observed after `launchctl bootout`: leader `false`, plain child `false`, `start_new_session` child `true`, double-fork daemon `true`.
- Artifact SHA-256: `acafbb461d09fa248b7637aeeefe9740fd0edd15789acff1e42f595296185d3a`.

This proves launchd/process-group-only cleanup is not sufficient.

### After: exact-head lease cleanup

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` proof pinned to `457208666c72cd58b3fa6a39195de3f9c98dfa3c`:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29184382185
- Candidate job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29184382185/job/86627747180
- Baseline job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29184382185/job/86627747153
- ACPX process/runtime/service suites: 4 files, 99 tests passed.
- Real detached lease test: reparented descendant discovered by inherited lease identity and reaped.
- ACP manager cancellation: 1 file, 3 tests passed, including protocol-cancel failure and close/drain failure paths.
- Abort/operator feedback: 1 file, 33 tests passed, including containment-failure reporting.
- Candidate proof logs were uploaded as the `openclaw-104929-candidate-proof` artifact.

### Service-managed ownership proof

Public GitHub-hosted `macos-14` launchd service proof pinned to `457208666c72cd58b3fa6a39195de3f9c98dfa3c`:

- Run: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29185025005
- Job: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29185025005/job/86629458125
- Artifact: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29185025005/artifacts/8257721358
- Artifact SHA-256: `c8b056f63ef9a3c876734583447935bb81cf63ea5c4562bd28fea930ef3a0bb1`.
- Before abort: launchd service `true`, lease-owned reparented descendant `true`, unrelated persistent background `true`.
- After abort: launchd service `true`, lease-owned descendant `false`, unrelated persistent background `true`.
- Cleanup result: the leased PID was inspected and terminated; no `survivingPids` were reported.
- The workflow uses `set -o pipefail` for every evidence pipeline so harness failures cannot be hidden by `tee`.

### Full CI

- Final candidate CI: https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29184421948
- Passed on exact head: docs, production types, test types, lint, extension-package boundary, auto-reply/agent-runner shard, and all ACPX-focused proof lanes.
- The full run also reports three unrelated existing UI/bundle failures (`checks-ui`, `build-artifacts`, `checks-node-core-runtime-media-ui`); this PR changes no UI, locale, or bundle artifact paths.
- Upstream PR checks: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104929/checks
- Local lightweight preflight: targeted `oxfmt`, targeted `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed. Builds and test suites run in GitHub Actions.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- Real POSIX detached/reparented lease cleanup.
- Lease environment matching with Gateway-instance isolation.
- TERM-resistant process escalation and survivor reporting.
- Windows process-inventory parsing.
- Runtime close failure marks a lease lost and propagates failure.
- Startup fails closed when a stale lease survives.
- Active cancellation closes and evicts the runtime handle even when protocol cancellation fails.
- `/stop` returns containment failure instead of false success.

## Risk And Rollback

- Cancellation now closes the live ACP runtime handle; the next turn may need to reopen/resume it.
- POSIX process inventory is bounded to 8 MiB and is not logged. Inventory failure is treated as an unverified cleanup, not success.
- A stale lease that cannot drain prevents ACPX backend startup rather than allowing an unverified worker to coexist with the new Gateway.
- Windows cleanup remains PID/PPID based because inherited environment inventory is not available through `Win32_Process`.
- Reverting this commit restores the previous cancel/session reuse and PPID-only cleanup behavior.

## Not Tested

- No private Claude credentials or paid-provider runtime were used. Public CI uses deterministic real host processes and the production ACPX lease/reaper/control-plane implementation.
